non-anonymous but the mock has no author. The backend always records the author of non-anonymous feedback and shows it; inventing one or making it anonymous would misrepresent it.

unsupported.reason: The mock stores a total only, not who acknowledged. An acknowledgement is an attestation by a named person, so none are invented; totals start at 0.
Metadata only in the mock; each database row needs a storageKey for a real stored file, and no files or file URLs are invented. Kept in seed-data.json under "unsupported".
The mock stores a total only, not who reacted; no reactions are attributed to people. Totals start at 0.

unsupported.entity: TeamActivity.rsvps of employees without an account
unsupported.reason: An RSVP is stored per membership. Employees who have no account for any other reason are not given one just to carry an RSVP, so those RSVPs are not seeded; RSVP totals are lower than in the mock.
Member totals are computed from CommunityMember rows; no accounts are invented to match them.
Personality affinity for social recommendations has no database column.
Attendee totals are computed from EventAttendee rows; no attendee accounts are invented. Seeded events start with 0 attendees.

notSeeded.entity: Career content (missions, challenges, courses, achievements, assessment questions)
notSeeded.reason: Already in backend/api/prisma/content/career.json, loaded with `pnpm --filter @grooveli/api db:content`. Identical to the frontend fixtures except one deliberate wording change (achievement "ach-first-app" drops "(simulated)").
The mock has no overrides; the backend falls back to DEFAULT_TIER_MODULES, which matches the frontend exactly.
The backend reports every game "coming-soon" when no row exists, matching the frontend. Titles and descriptions are static frontend copy.
Frontend-owned 3D placement; buildings find their organisation by id, which the seed keeps unchanged.
Analytics are computed by the backend from live records; there is no table for historical series.

notSeeded.entity: Payroll previews, XP events, challenge attempts, assistant messages, presence, market rates
notSeeded.reason: Empty in the mock initial state and/or backend-generated (authoritative XP, simulated payroll results, AI output, live presence, provider data). None are invented.

notSeeded.entity: Sessions, auth tokens, audit log, password hashes
notSeeded.reason: Never seeded. Accounts are locked until provisioned (see BACKEND_HANDOFF.md).

transformations: Organization.tier/workflows/setupChecklist come from the private workspace mock where one exists (2 of 9); the other organisations use the backend defaults (starter, no workflows, empty checklist).
Organization.leaveAllowances uses the frontend's LEAVE_ALLOWANCE ({"annual":25,"sick":10,"parental":60,"study":5,"unpaid":30}), which differs from the database default.

Employee accounts follow least privilege: only 7 of 42 HR records get an account and membership: the employee persona, plus the 6 recognition senders (Recognition.fromUserId is required). Every other record stays an HR record without a login; the backend supports that (Employee.userId is optional).
Demo candidate: CandidateProfile takes the profile fixture plus the mock privacy settings. The account is seeded as onboarded so the candidate flows can be tested straight away.

TalentProfile → User + CandidateProfile: qualifications → certifications; expectedSalary/workModes/employmentTypes/location → preferences; visibility "employers" (talent search); not listed in Social → People, as in the mock.

SocialProfile → CandidateProfile (headline, avatar, district → homeDistrict, interests), visibility "private" so social-only people stay out of employer talent search. Kofi Asante and Grace Ayodele are each one account across their social profile and organisation roles.

Employee memberships carry the single role "employee" (directory, engagement participation, self-service). The employee persona keeps its mock roles employee + manager, which the backend limits to the persona's direct reports.

Invitation.tokenHash is generated by PostgreSQL at execution time from random data, so nobody holds the raw token: seeded invitations can be listed and revoked, not accepted (as in the mock). expiresAt = sentAt + 7 days (the backend TTL).
Application.simulated is frontend-only and dropped; Application.source = "candidate".
Assessment.results gain reviewerId (matched by reviewer name) and at (seed time), which the database stores and the mock does not.
PerformanceReview.reviewerName is kept; reviewerId is set only when the reviewer has an account (most reviewers are HR records without one).

Pay components and salary structures are global in the mock but per-organisation in the database (ids are primary keys), so each is copied for every organisation with compensation data (amberline-health, kestrel-systems) with the organisation code appended (pc-housing → pc-housing-k). Compensation.structureId and CompensationStructure.componentIds are remapped the same way.

Survey responses become SurveyResponse rows without a user (the mock responses have no author, and anonymous responses never store one or a timestamp). No SurveyRespondent markers are written: they are HMACs keyed by the backend HASH_SECRET and the mock responses belong to no account. Seeded users can therefore still answer the surveys.
TeamActivity.rsvps hold employee ids in the mock; the database stores membership ids, so each is mapped through the employee → membership link (only for employees with an account).
CommunityPost ids are prefixed with their community id (p1 → com-builders-p1): the mock reuses p1, p2 … in every community, but the database id is global.

Community post authors ("Kofi A.") are matched to social-profile accounts by first name and last initial and become community members (the API only lets members post). authorName keeps the mock display text.
CityEvent.createdById = the host organisation's org-admin account when there is one, otherwise the platform account.
Notification n-welcome: body rewritten; the mock text says data is "stored only in this browser", which is untrue once it is in the database.
